title: If Organic Food Was Honest - Honest Ads
summary: Satirical Honest Ads sketch mocking organic marketing, natural pesticides, fraud and the lack of health benefits.

assertions.quote: healthwise organic food actually has no measurable leg up on the competition
organic produce accounts for 8% of ecoli outbreaks despite being just 1% of the food supply

verdicts.note: Systematic review (abstract only): E. coli contamination risk did not differ between organic and conventional produce.
Organic standards permit certain plant or microbial extracts and copper- and sulfur-based crop protection products.
Of 385 pesticide substances authorised in the EU, 26 are also approved for organic agriculture, including pyrethrins and copper.

7 CFR 205.206(e) lets organic producers apply biological or botanical substances or National List synthetics to control pests, weeds and diseases when cultural, mechanical and physical methods are not enough, so organic farming does use pesticides.

USDA's report states that organic agriculture uses permitted pest-control materials, mostly naturally derived (pyrethrum, Bt) plus a few synthetics such as sulfur, insecticidal soap, horticultural oils and copper hydroxide.

assertions.quote: if you ate organic grains between 2010 and 2017 there's a good chance that no you didn't

verdicts.note: USDA bought 571 USDA-organic samples of six produce items at retail in 2010-11: 57% had no detected residue, 39% traces under the 5%-of-tolerance allowance and 4% were in violation, only some of them likely mislabeled conventional; the study notes it was not a probability sample, covers six commodities and residue testing cannot see fraud that leaves no residue.

Baden-Wuerttemberg's state lab judged 0% of fresh organic produce falsely labelled in 2021 (always well under 5% in 2011-2020, up to 8.5% before 2010) and 3.1% of processed organic foods (2.2-7.0% in recent years, over 8% before 2011); a German market and residue-based detection only, with targeted projects limiting year-to-year comparison.
